performance.candidate_source_note: Paired run predates the final prepared-exec credential/auxv dependency fix. The separate 45-sample confirmation uses the final committed runtime and installed Dev binary.

performance_interpretation: Five alternating before/candidate pairs per CPU count and mode; 5000 calls per thread. Final confirmation is after-only and is not a new paired comparison.
Timed region starts after threads are created and TSYNC completes, and ends when all workers finish. Joins are outside the timer.
Large denied-call gain removes repeated cohort returns; it is not a Firefox or Geekbench result.
Native macOS only supports the unfiltered control here; the Linux reference is a native ARM64 Linux-kernel CI guest with six provisioned CPUs, so twelve threads are oversubscribed.
Native references use different kernels, page sizes and scheduling; no CPU pinning. Short controls do not establish a general speedup or zero regression.
Final 4/12-CPU diagnostic logs have no denied getppid or TSYNC cohort-return entries and zero compatibility-service requests. Other allowed calls retain their underlying fallback.
corrected_failures: An existing shared-custody test dropped its channel receiver while a callback copied before unsubscribe could still send. Keep the receiver alive through unlock/join; the actual wake assertion remains.
Early child signal binding used the parent PID namespace. Bind after child namespace activation; existing old-TID retention regression passes.

Late TSYNC NNP could leave a prepared setuid exec privileged. Refresh credentials/capabilities and retained plus initial-stack auxv under original group custody without re-reading executable metadata.
The benchmark initially required getppid > 0; guest init legitimately has parent 0. The corrected control accepts nonnegative results; all recorded final samples use that fixture.
validation_reuse: Mac full runtime workflow passed before the final exec dependency fix. Linux workflow initially stopped at the shared test receiver lifetime failure: retain the failed summary, reuse already-passed checks, and rerun the failed and remaining suites/doc tests/build steps.
